context: A 5-person startup (Series A, 18-month runway) runs 12 microservices on Kubernetes. They currently have basic logging (stdout to CloudWatch) and uptime monitoring (Pingdom). They need distributed tracing, metrics dashboards, alerting, and log aggregation to debug a growing number of cross-service issues that take hours to diagnose. Options: (A) Buy — adopt Datadog (~$1,500/month at current scale, scaling to ~$5,000/month projected), 1 week integration. (B) Build — self-host Grafana + Prometheus + Jaeger + Loki on their existing Kubernetes cluster, 3-4 weeks to set up, $200/month infrastructure. The CTO prefers self-hosting because 'we control our destiny and it's cheaper.' One engineer has Prometheus experience. The company processes sensitive healthcare data (HIPAA compliance).
question: Should the startup build (self-host open-source observability stack) or buy (adopt Datadog)?
expert_answer: Buy (Datadog). The cost difference ($1,300/month net) is negligible relative to engineer-time opportunity cost and compliance risk.
expert_reasoning: The 5-person team's scarcest resource is engineering time, not money ($1,500/month is ~3% of a single engineer's fully loaded cost). Self-hosting requires 3-4 weeks upfront PLUS ongoing maintenance: Prometheus storage scaling, Grafana dashboard maintenance, Jaeger sampling tuning, Loki index management, and Kubernetes resource allocation for the observability stack itself. This maintenance burden falls on the one engineer with Prometheus experience, creating a bus factor of 1 for a critical system. The HIPAA dimension adds another layer: self-hosted observability tools that process request traces containing PHI must be configured for compliance (encryption at rest, access controls, audit logging, data retention policies). Datadog has a HIPAA-eligible offering with a BAA. Building equivalent compliance controls into a self-hosted stack is weeks of additional work and ongoing audit burden. The CTO's 'control our destiny' argument trades $1,300/month for 4+ weeks of setup, ongoing maintenance load, compliance risk, and a key-person dependency — all during a period when the team should be shipping product to extend their 18-month runway.
anti_pattern: Self-hosting because 'it is cheaper on paper.' This compares monthly infrastructure cost ($200 vs $1,500) while ignoring the dominant cost: engineer time. 4 weeks of setup = ~$15,000 in engineer salary alone, which takes 11 months to recoup at $1,300/month savings. Adding ongoing maintenance (conservatively 4 hours/week = $500/week) eliminates the savings entirely. The decision optimizes for the visible cost (vendor bill) while ignoring the invisible costs (opportunity cost, maintenance burden, compliance risk, bus factor).
